name: removed_block_comment
description: A sub-block was removed from inside a function and a developer-style ONE-LINER comment now marks the site; the target re-inserts the removed block verbatim. Corpus side: normalized CRAN functions with 6+ body lines (highest version per package, the build_astfim versions.json cache pattern); ONE strictly interior run of consecutive top-level statements (3-8 lines, tree-sitter statement boundaries - a guard clause, a computation stanza - never the whole body) is cut out. Prompt: file window + the function down to the removal site, then the comment line + cursor; suffix = the post-block remainder of the function through its closing brace plus a file-below window (scope-aware-context rule). The comment itself is the ONE LLM call per row (backend agy, zai fallback): the 5-style pool from comment_to_code as templates, prompted with the removed block, asked for how a dev would jot it - meaningful intent, NOT a complete spec, no code, max 80 chars. Validation: corpus-exact target text, comment length/format gate, and a tree-sitter floor that the target re-parses as clean R statements.
novelty_note: comment_to_code_styles puts a generated comment above an INTACT block the model must then write - the comment describes code that is about to appear for the first time. Here the block is GONE (removed from a real function), the comment is the only trace a returning developer leaves at the site, and the model must reconstruct the exact removed code from function context + suffix + one-line intent. It is the remove-then-reinsert inverse of astfim_partial's retyping: no typed partial exists, only the jot-note. Nothing existing trains reconstruction of deleted code from a dev's site marker; the exact gate stays corpus-side (region_new = verbatim removed lines) while the single LLM call is confined to the comment (comment_prefix construction, r_comment_gate validator).
